items.stem: Which organelle is the primary site of cellular respiration, releasing energy the cell can use?
options: Mitochondrion
Ribosome
Golgi apparatus
Vacuole

items.stem: A cell's membrane controls what enters and leaves, its ribosomes build proteins, and its mitochondria supply energy. This coordinated activity best shows how organelles —
options: compete with one another for limited space
work together as a system to maintain homeostasis
each carry out every cell function independently
function only during cell division
items.answer_text: work together as a system to maintain homeostasis

items.stem: How does mitosis differ from meiosis?
options: Meiosis produces two cells identical to the parent cell
Mitosis produces four unique gametes used for reproduction
Mitosis makes identical cells; meiosis makes varied gametes
Both processes always produce cells with doubled chromosome numbers
items.answer_text: Mitosis makes identical cells; meiosis makes varied gametes

items.stem: Binary fission in bacteria and mitosis in your skin cells both maintain genetic continuity because each —
options: reduces the chromosome number by half each cycle
requires two parent organisms in order to occur
copies the DNA so the new cells match the parent
produces gametes that are later used in fertilization
items.answer_text: copies the DNA so the new cells match the parent

items.stem: Which type of macromolecule stores hereditary information and directs protein synthesis?
options: Nucleic acid
Carbohydrate
Lipid
Phospholipid

items.stem: A freshwater plant cell is placed in very salty water. What will happen to the water in the cell?
options: Water will move into the cell, causing it to swell
Water will stay balanced because the cell is isotonic
Water will move out of the cell, causing it to shrink
Water will stop moving across the membrane entirely
items.answer_text: Water will move out of the cell, causing it to shrink

items.stem: Which process moves molecules from an area of high concentration to low concentration WITHOUT using cellular energy?
options: Active transport
Endocytosis
Exocytosis
Diffusion

items.stem: Which statement best describes the relationship between photosynthesis and cellular respiration?
options: Both processes release oxygen as a waste product
The products of one process are the reactants of the other
Both processes occur only in animal cells
Respiration stores energy while photosynthesis releases it
items.answer_text: The products of one process are the reactants of the other

items.stem: The repeating subunits (monomers) that make up a molecule of DNA are called —
options: nucleotides
amino acids
fatty acids
monosaccharides

items.stem: During which process is the information in DNA used to build a molecule of messenger RNA (mRNA)?
options: Replication
Translation
Digestion
Transcription

items.stem: A change in the sequence of DNA bases, sometimes caused by radiation or certain chemicals, is called a —
options: fertilization
dominant trait
phenotype
mutation

items.stem: Crossing over during meiosis increases genetic variation because it —
options: makes exact copies of each chromosome for the gametes
swaps segments between homologous chromosomes
lowers the total number of genes found in a cell
stops fertilization from being able to take place

items.stem: Which is an ethical concern often raised about using biotechnology such as genetically modified crops?
options: Modified crops can never increase how much food is produced
DNA can never be moved between two different organisms
The process always removes all genetic variation from crops
Possible long-term effects on health are still debated
items.answer_text: Possible long-term effects on health are still debated

items.stem: Mendel's law of segregation is explained by which event during meiosis?
options: Alleles separating into different gametes
The copying of all the DNA before the cell divides
Two gametes joining together during fertilization
Chromosomes being copied in ordinary body cells

items.stem: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant to short (t). If two Tt plants are crossed, what fraction of the offspring are expected to be short?
options: 0 (none)

items.stem: In four-o'clock flowers, red (R) and white (W) alleles show incomplete dominance, so RW plants are pink. Crossing two pink plants gives offspring in about what ratio?
options: all pink
1 red : 2 pink : 1 white
3 red : 1 white
all red

items.stem: Which is an advantage of asexual reproduction compared with sexual reproduction?
options: It produces much greater genetic variation
A single parent can reproduce quickly
Offspring are better able to adapt to change
It requires two parents and more total energy
items.answer_text: A single parent can reproduce quickly

items.stem: The theory of endosymbiosis explains the origin of mitochondria and chloroplasts by proposing that they —
options: developed from inward folds of the cell membrane over time
split off from the cell's nucleus a very long time ago
were once free-living bacteria taken in by a host cell
are built only out of nucleic acids
items.answer_text: were once free-living bacteria taken in by a host cell

items.stem: Which group of organisms is made of cells that LACK a membrane-bound nucleus?
options: Animals
Plants
Bacteria
Fungi

items.stem: On a cladogram, two species whose branches share the most recent common ancestor are —
options: the most distantly related
unrelated to all other species
identical in every trait
the most closely related

items.stem: Why do many scientists argue that viruses are NOT truly living organisms?
options: They contain genetic material
They are made of proteins
They cannot reproduce without a host cell
They are able to cause diseases
items.answer_text: They cannot reproduce without a host cell

items.stem: Two species are found to have very similar DNA and protein sequences. This is best used as evidence that they —
options: live in the same habitat
share a common ancestor
are the same species
do not evolve at all

items.stem: The largest population size that an environment can support over time is called its —
options: carrying capacity
biodiversity
keystone species
limiting factor

items.stem: Which is a density-dependent limiting factor for a growing deer population?
options: Disease spreading as the population grows
An unusually severe drought during the winter
A fast-moving forest fire in the area
A sudden drop in the outdoor temperature
items.answer_text: Disease spreading as the population grows

items.stem: A keystone species is best described as one that —
options: is the single largest organism found in its ecosystem
is always the top predator in a food web
simply lives longer than the other species do
strongly affects its ecosystem despite low numbers
items.answer_text: strongly affects its ecosystem despite low numbers

items.stem: In an energy pyramid, the amount of energy available at each higher level —
options: decreases
increases
stays exactly the same
disappears completely

items.stem: A disease kills most of the producers in a food web. What is the most immediate effect on the primary consumers?
options: They increase rapidly in number
They become producers themselves
They lose their main source of food
They gain more available energy
items.answer_text: They lose their main source of food

items.stem: Which statement best explains why decomposers are essential in an ecosystem?
options: They make most of the oxygen in the air
They give energy directly to the sun
They keep matter from cycling at all
They return nutrients to the soil
items.answer_text: They return nutrients to the soil

items.stem: A greater variety of species (high biodiversity) usually makes an ecosystem more stable because it —
options: prevents any change from ever occurring
guarantees that no species will ever go extinct
removes all competition among the organisms
provides more ways to recover from disturbance
items.answer_text: provides more ways to recover from disturbance

items.stem: Which human action would most directly REDUCE the negative impact of humans on the environment?
options: Clearing large areas of forest for new farmland
Releasing a non-native fish into a lake
Restoring wetlands and native plants
Burning more fossil fuels to produce energy

items.stem: Introducing a non-native (invasive) species to an ecosystem often reduces biodiversity because the invader —
options: almost always dies off very quickly
increases the food supply for every species
has many natural predators already present
outcompetes native species for resources

items.stem: An organism is MOST likely to survive an environmental change if it —
options: completely stops reproducing during the change
can tolerate the new conditions with its traits
carries no genetic variation at all in its population
happens to be the largest member of its species
items.answer_text: can tolerate the new conditions with its traits

items.stem: A population grows quickly and then levels off near a steady size. The leveling off happens because the population has —
options: run out of every resource all at once
no limiting factors acting on it
permanently stopped reproducing
reached its carrying capacity

items.stem: New understandings of Earth's great age and the fossil record influenced biology mainly by —
options: supporting the idea that species change over time
proving that species can never change at all
showing that Earth is only a few thousand years old
disproving everything that is known about genetics
items.answer_text: supporting the idea that species change over time

items.stem: Speciation, the formation of new species over time, tends to increase an area's —
options: extinction rate only
biodiversity
age of the Earth
average body size

items.stem: The forelimbs of humans, whales, and bats all share the same basic bone arrangement. These homologous structures are evidence of —
options: identical environments
common ancestry
completely different genetic codes
unrelated origins

items.stem: Which additional finding would BEST support the claim that two species share a common ancestor?
options: They have very similar DNA and protein sequences
They happen to live on the same continent
They are about the same color
They are hunted by the same predator
items.answer_text: They have very similar DNA and protein sequences

items.stem: Genetic drift differs from natural selection because genetic drift —
options: changes allele frequencies by chance
always improves an organism's survival
occurs only in very large populations
never changes a population at all

items.stem: Repeated use of an antibiotic can produce a resistant bacterial population because the antibiotic —
options: causes the bacteria to mutate on purpose each time
teaches the bacteria how to become stronger
lets resistant bacteria survive and reproduce
has no real effect on the bacteria at all
items.answer_text: lets resistant bacteria survive and reproduce

items.stem: In natural selection, which individuals are most likely to pass their traits to the next generation?
options: The largest individuals in the group
The youngest individuals in the group
Those best suited to their environment
Those that reproduce the least often
items.answer_text: Those best suited to their environment
